subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: When two objects are in thermal equilibrium, they have the same:
questions.explain: Thermal equilibrium means no net heat flow, which occurs when temperatures are equal.

questions.q: The internal energy of a substance increases during melting even though temperature is constant because:
options: Potential energy of particles rises as bonds break
Both kinetic and potential energy rise
questions.explain: Latent heat increases particle potential energy as bonds break, with no temperature change.

questions.q: A brittle material is one that:
options: Breaks suddenly with little or no plastic deformation
Undergoes large plastic deformation before breaking
questions.explain: Brittle materials (e.g. glass) fracture abruptly with negligible plastic deformation.

questions.q: A force–extension graph for a metal wire shows a straight line then curves over before fracture. The straight portion corresponds to:
questions.explain: The initial straight-line region is the elastic region where Hooke's law holds.

questions.q: For an ideal gas, the internal energy depends only on:
questions.explain: An ideal gas has no intermolecular potential energy, so internal energy depends only on temperature.

questions.q: The root-mean-square (rms) speed of gas molecules is found by:
options: Taking the square root of the mean of the squared speeds
questions.explain: The rms speed is √⟨c²⟩, the square root of the mean of the squared speeds.

questions.q: The elastic strain energy stored in a stretched material equals:
options: The gradient of the force–extension graph
The area under the force–extension graph
questions.explain: Work done in stretching, and hence energy stored, equals the area under the force–extension graph.

questions.q: Tensile strain is defined as:
questions.explain: Strain ε = extension ÷ original length and is a dimensionless ratio.

questions.q: Temperature is a measure of the:
options: Total internal energy of a body
Average random kinetic energy of the particles
questions.explain: Absolute temperature is proportional to the average random kinetic energy of particles.

questions.q: If the absolute temperature of an ideal gas is doubled, the rms speed of its molecules:
questions.explain: Since ½m⟨c²⟩ ∝ T, the rms speed ∝ √T, so it increases by √2.

questions.q: A material is described as 'stiff' if it has a:
questions.explain: Stiffness corresponds to a high Young modulus: large stress produces only small strain.

questions.q: The specific latent heat of vaporisation is generally larger than that of fusion because:
options: Vaporisation occurs at a higher temperature
Separating particles fully and doing work against the atmosphere needs more energy
Gases have higher specific heat capacity
questions.explain: Vaporisation requires breaking nearly all intermolecular bonds and work against the atmosphere.

questions.q: A temperature of 27 °C expressed in kelvin is:
On a stress–strain graph, the Young modulus is given by:
options: The gradient of the initial linear (straight-line) region
questions.explain: E equals the gradient of the linear (Hooke's-law) part of the stress–strain graph.

questions.q: Plastic deformation is characterised by:
options: A permanent change in shape after the load is removed
questions.explain: Plastic deformation leaves a permanent extension once the load is removed.

questions.q: When a wire is loaded only up to its limit of proportionality and then unloaded, the loading and unloading lines on a force–extension graph:
questions.explain: Within the elastic (proportional) region, loading and unloading follow the same straight line.

questions.q: Which is NOT an assumption of the kinetic theory of an ideal gas?
options: Molecules exert strong attractive forces on each other except during collisions
Molecules are in continuous random motion
The volume of molecules is negligible compared with the gas volume
questions.explain: Kinetic theory assumes negligible intermolecular forces except during collisions, not strong ones.

questions.q: A spring extends 0.040 m when a force of 8.0 N is applied. Its spring constant is:
In the ideal gas equation pV = nRT, the temperature T must be measured in:
questions.explain: pV = nRT requires the absolute (Kelvin) temperature.

questions.q: Two wires of the same material but different lengths and areas are tested. The Young modulus is:
options: The same for both, since it is a property of the material
questions.explain: The Young modulus is an intrinsic material property, independent of the specimen's dimensions.

questions.q: The mean kinetic energy of a molecule in an ideal gas is given by:
questions.explain: Mean translational kinetic energy per molecule is (3/2)kT.

questions.q: A spring of constant 50 N m⁻¹ is extended by 0.20 m. The elastic strain energy stored is:
The spring constant k represents:
options: The stiffness — force needed per unit extension
questions.explain: k is the stiffness, the force required to produce unit extension (N m⁻¹).

questions.q: A fixed mass of gas at 2.0 × 10⁵ Pa and 300 K is heated at constant volume to 600 K. The new pressure is:
questions.explain: At constant volume p ∝ T, so doubling T doubles p to 4.0 × 10⁵ Pa.

questions.q: The SI unit of the Young modulus is the same as that of:
questions.explain: Strain is dimensionless, so the Young modulus has the units of stress, the pascal.

questions.q: Hooke's law states that, up to the limit of proportionality:
options: Extension is proportional to the applied force
Force is inversely proportional to extension
questions.explain: Hooke's law: extension is directly proportional to the applied force, F = kx.

questions.q: A steel wire and a rubber band are both stretched. Compared with steel, rubber typically has a:
questions.explain: Rubber is far more easily stretched than steel, so it has a much lower Young modulus.

questions.q: A real gas behaves most like an ideal gas at:
questions.explain: At low pressure and high temperature molecules are far apart with negligible interactions.

questions.q: Density is defined as:
questions.explain: Density ρ = mass ÷ volume, with units kg m⁻³.

questions.q: The kelvin and Celsius scales differ by:
questions.explain: T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15; the scales have the same size of degree but differ by an offset.
